$comment: JobScout design system v3 — the single source of truth.
Nothing in this file is a hex code, a px size or a duration chosen by hand.
Everything is a CONSTANT or a FORMULA INPUT. tokens/generate.mjs turns this
into tokens.css, Tokens.kt and Tokens.swift, and tools/check_tokens.mjs
proves the three generated files still agree with it.
Why this file exists: three of the six subsystems were already generative
and had never been written down (colour, motion, rose geometry), and three
were hand-tuned and had drifted (type: 20 distinct sizes between 8 and 31px;
space: 17 distinct values; elevation: no constant rung). See
docs/DESIGN-ALGORITHM.md for the measurements.
MEASURED: the shipped product uses 20 distinct sizes between 8 and 31px.
A 1.10 ratio 'fits' them at 0.41px RMS, which proves nothing — at that
ratio every number is near a step. There was no scale.
This is one: base 9, ratio 1.195, eight steps, rounded to 0.5px. It lands
within 0.5px of every role the product actually uses, and it replaces 20
sizes with 8.

roles.t0: caps label — band pill, evidence key, section label

type.$familyLaw: serif 400 for titles (t4-t7) only; sans for everything else; mono tabular for every numeral that is data.

$comment: MEASURED: 17 distinct values from 1 to 26px. Snapping to a 4px grid with
one half-step moves nothing by more than 2px — verified by render.
One constant and one step. card = 16; everything else is 16 ± 6.
chip 4 · inner 10 · card 16 · sheet 22 · pill.
MEASURED, and the asymmetry is NOT a bug. On light, --surface is #ffffff
— the ceiling. A hover cannot go lighter, so light carries elevation in
shadow alone and --surface-hover equals --surface (1.000:1, measured).
On dark there is no shadow (a warm shadow on ink reads as dirt), so dark
carries it entirely in lift.
Two named steps replace the hand-picked rungs.
PROVEN: these 14 numbers regenerate all 24 shipped band colours —
22/24 byte-exact, 2 off by 1/255 rounding. The band ramp was always a
generator. NEAR-MISS is the same ramp at 0.28x chroma, which is why it
reads as the neutral: its band IS the neutral.
The product has exactly ONE neutral family: indigo 265-295, plus a warm
cream on light that is achromatic (C <= 0.019). PING (270) and NEAR-MISS
(285) live inside it by design. AUTO (147) and UNSURE (63) are the only
two hues outside it — the only two that mean something on sight.
This is the rule tools/check_scale.mjs enforces on large surfaces, and it
is why the ink hero passes at chroma 0.087 while a green one fails at
0.077: hue MEMBERSHIP is the test, not chroma magnitude.

market.$comment: RULING 2026-09-21 (Ken): the hero is market-driven and Kenya stays green. Hue 147 overlaps AUTO; raised, accepted, closed. Market colour appears on the hero and the market chip ONLY.

$comment: Already generative: each curve is a real damped-spring step response
sampled into linear(). The asymmetry law is the system: entries
340-520ms, exits 160ms, exits never overshoot.
CONFIRMED from the code 2026-09-21 (Claude Code): identical on web,
worker, mockup, Android and iOS. An earlier draft of js/band.js carried
69 and 55 as 45 — BOTH inferred boundaries were wrong.
They live here, not in band.js, for the same reason the band colours do:
the scorer emits `fit` ONLY and every client derives the band itself, so
there are five copies of this table today. Generating it into CSS, Kotlin
and Swift makes them one copy with five readers.
